Build the roxygen2-generation prompt from an sd_data object

Source: R/roxygen.R
sd_check_object_name_.Rd

Turns the metadata already attached to an sd_data object (variable labels, value labels, missing counts, dataset-level paradata) into the full text prompt that sd_generate_roxygen() sends to the language model. Kept separate from sd_generate_roxygen() so the prompt can be inspected or unit-tested without needing Ollama (or any model) running — the same idea as sd_build_prompt() for sd_document().

Usage

sd_check_object_name_(object_name)

Arguments

object_name

Name the documented object will have once saved with usethis::use_data(), e.g. "survey_data". Written into the generated roxygen2 block as the final line (the line that normally follows a dataset's documentation and names the object it documents).

x

An sd_data object.

instructions

Character string with the instructions placed before the dataset information. NULL (the default) uses a built-in instruction template (see language) asking for a roxygen2 block following the usual @format/@details/@source structure for a documented dataset.

language

Language of the built-in instructions template (and of the small field labels in the dataset-information block, e.g. "Label"/"Type"/"Missing") when instructions is left at its default NULL – one of "fi" (Finnish, the default), "en" (English) or "sv" (Swedish). Has no effect when instructions is supplied explicitly. Independent of the language the survey data itself (variable labels etc.) happens to be in – see sd_build_prompt() for the same idea applied to sd_document().

context

Optional character string of retrieved background material to insert before the dataset information – typically the output of sd_retrieve_context(). NULL (the default) omits this section entirely, leaving the prompt exactly as before this parameter was added.

Value

A single character string: the full prompt.

Details

Only metadata is included (labels, value labels, per-variable missing counts, dataset-level paradata) — never the raw data values themselves, so open-text responses are never sent to the model.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aineisto <- sd_read("survey_data.csv")
kehote <- sd_build_roxygen_prompt(aineisto, "survey_data")
cat(kehote)

# Englanninkielinen roxygen-dokumentaatio samasta aineistosta:
kehote_en <- sd_build_roxygen_prompt(aineisto, "survey_data", language = "en")

# RAG-taustatiedolla:
store <- ragnar::ragnar_store_connect("oma_rag_store.ragnar.duckdb")
kehote_rag <- sd_build_roxygen_prompt(
  aineisto, "survey_data",
  context = sd_retrieve_context(aineisto, store)
)
} # }
